newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: PM TO CALL EARLY NATIVE TITLE MEETING
The Prime Minister is to call an early meeting of State and Territory Leaders to discuss native title issues.
Mr Howard made the announcement after another round of talks today with Aboriginal groups aimed at brokering a response to the High Court's Wik judgement.
The Prime Minister says while considerable progress has been achieved, several important issues require further discussion, and a further meeting's been arranged for Thursday.
A spokesman for Mr Howard says the Prime Minister wants to consult Premiers and Chief Ministers before revealing the Federal Government's position on native title.
The meeting with State and Territory leaders is unlikely to be held until at least next week, further delaying the Government's Wik response.
BEAZLEY WELCOMES PM'S DECISION TO KEEP NATIVE TITLE
Federal Opposition leader, Kim Beazley, says while he welcomes the Prime Minister's decision not to wipe out Native Title he can't guarantee support for Mr Howard's plan.
Mr Beazley says there are still a lot more issues to consider in the legislation than just extinguishment.
Mr Howard says he's not proposing a blanket extinguishment of Native Title over pastoral leases but will deliver security to farmers.
PROBLEM GAMBLING IN ETHNIC COMMUNITIES
Head of the New South Wales Council on Problem Gambling says reasearch needs to be done on problem gambling in non-English speaking communities in Australia.
Paul Symond believes problem gambling is as high or higher in those communities than in the general community.
Mr Symond says the incidence of compulsive gambling in ethnic groups is virtually unexplored, but anecdotal evidence suggests it is higher.
He says the opening of the Sydney Casino has compounded the problem because only small amounts of English-language skills are required to gamble.
WESTPAC DEFENDS SMALL BUSINESS LENDING
The head of Westpac has defended banks for their record on small business lending.
The Federal Treasurer and the Prime Minister have both criticised banks for not supporting small business.
After the release of the Wallis report, they said the big four banks won't be allowed to merge until there was more competition in banking, particularly in small business lending.
Speaking at a Sydney business lunch today, Westpac managing director, Robert Joss said banks were very competitive with comparitively low profit margins in small business lending.
SCHOOLS NEED TO DO MORE FOR JOB SEEKERS: KEMP
Federal Schools Minister, David Kemp, says his plan for secondary schools to find jobs for students will allow them to do more to help the students not going on to university or full-time TAFE.

Under the scheme, which is part of the project to replace the Commonwealth Employment Service, schools will be paid a commission, depending on how many students they match with jobs. Dr Kemp says there's no danger of schools being converted into job centres.
VITAL NEWS ON PERTH GIRL'S FINAL MOVEMENTS
In Perth, police hunting the killer of Ciara Glennon say the victim was last seen on the Stirling Highway about 15 minutes after she left a hotel in Clarement.
Ciara is one of three girls who've disappeared from the Claremont nightclub strip in the past 16 months, and police believe they're hunting a serial killer.
They say Ciara was seen standing on the Highway near the Taste of Thai Restaurant at 12.15am on March the 15th, and appeared to be waiting for a vehicle, possibly a taxi.
Detective Inspector Dave Caporn says the 27-year-old lawyer was anxious to get home and in an error of judgement, may have accepted a lift from a stranger.
Police have so far interviewed more than one-thousand people who were in the Claremont area the night Ciara disappeared.
-- Reuter Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
